observation.visible_scene: A bright indoor dance studio with a full-height wall mirror, rows of ceiling light fixtures and stage lamps, a ballet barre, white sheer curtains, windows on the right, a folded blue mat at far right, and a red bolster plus a black mat on the floor near the mirror. A single dancer in a dark ink-wash-patterned top and black pants, hair in a bun, stands right-of-center performing with a large folding fan that has long gradient (white-to-teal/gray) silk streamers attached. Her mirrored image appears to her left across the mirror plane and moves in sync; it is a reflection, not a second person. The camera is static throughout.
visible_changes: The fan is already extended horizontally to the dancer's left at t=0 and continues to be manipulated through the whole excerpt, with no clear start or end pose.

The dancer repeatedly opens the fan into a spread white disc (e.g., t≈0.53, 0.87, 1.60, 2.33) and closes/turns it edge-on, while the long streamers alternately arc overhead, drape across her head, hang vertically, or trail to the side.

Fan height cycles: held high overhead (t≈0.13–0.67), lowered near the waist/legs as she crouches or bends forward (t≈0.73–1.00), raised vertically in front and overhead (t≈1.07–1.47), extended to the side (t≈1.53–1.60), and swept overhead again (t≈1.67 onward).
Body posture changes with the fan work: upright with one arm raised, a slight forward bend/crouch when the fan is low, and turning weight shifts with a lifted leg around t≈1.80–1.93.
The mirror reflection reproduces every posture and fan change, flipped left-right, confirming a single moving dancer rather than two.
Background elements (lights, barre, curtains, windows, blue mat, red bolster, black mat) remain fixed in frame position across all samples, indicating no camera pan or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: The choreography before t=0 and after the last frame, the accompanying music, and the intended phrase or completion of the fan sequence are not shown.
Whether the repeated overhead sweeps belong to one continuous spin or to separate choreographic beats cannot be determined from this cropped segment.
uncertain_details: Exact fan open/closed state at each transition is hard to read because the streamers occlude the fan face during fast swings.
The precise rotation angle of the dancer's turns is unclear; only partial weight shifts and a lifted leg are visible.
The material identity of the streamers and fan (silk, synthetic, etc.) is not verifiable from the frames.
